questions.stem: The lock and key model explains enzyme specificity. What does this model suggest?

options.text: Enzymes can work on any substrate
Substrates change the shape of the enzyme permanently
Enzymes lock onto cells and break them apart
The enzyme's active site has a specific shape that only fits one type of substrate molecule

questions.explanation: The lock and key model states that the active site of an enzyme has a specific shape that is complementary to only one substrate, just like a lock only accepts a specific key.
